newsitem.title: HONG KONG: CM Hai Hong details HK$3.8 bln investment.
newsitem.headline: CM Hai Hong details HK$3.8 bln investment.

text.p: China Merchants Hai Hong Holdings Ltd issued details of its planned acquisition of joint ventures projects from its parent and sister companies in a lengthy statement released on Thursday.
The company said it would acquire equity interests in five toll highways in China and a 23.32 percent stake in a Shenzhen-listed manufacturing company for a total of HK$3.86 billion.

The company would acquire the investments from parent China Merchants Holdings (Hong Kong) Ltd and sister companies China Merchants China Direct Investments Ltd (CMCDI) and Union Bank of Hong Kong Ltd.

The listed company would acquire from its parent China Merchants Holdings (Hong Kong) Ltd its 60 percent holding in each of two Sino-foreign equity joint ventures, the Ningzhenluo joint ventures, which hold the operating rights of the Ningzhenluo Highway in Zhejiang province, the statement said.
This toll road formed part of the road network linking Ningbo and Zhenhai on National Highway 329, and Ningbo with Hangzhou.
The venture, established in April 1997 with a 28-year term, had a total aggregate investment of about HK$271.71 million.

Hai Hong was also acquiring from its parent an 80 percent interest in each of 12 Sino-foreign cooperative joint ventures, the Guiliu joint ventures, which upon completion of construction will hold the operating rights of the Guiliu Highway in the Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region.
This toll road was expected to be operational by May 1997.
The joint venture was established in April 1997 and had a term of 25 years. The total aggregate investment of this project was HK$2.32 billion and the JV carried a guaranteed return.

Hai Hong would acquire from its parent a 60 percent economic interest in each of four Sino-foreign joint ventures, the Guihuang joint ventures, which would hold upon completion of construction the operating rights of the Guihuang Highway in Guizhou province, the statement said.
This toll road was to open in May 1997. The joint venture agreement had a term of 25 years, called for a total investment of about HK$841.40 million, and carried a guaranteed return.

China Merchants Hai Hong was acquiring from China Merchants China Direct Investments (CMCDI), a 16.8 percent economic interest in a Sino-foreign cooperative joint venture, the Zhangzhou joint venture, which held the operating rights of the Zhangzhou section of National Highway 324 in Fujian province.
The joint venture, which was set up April 1992, had a term of 30 years and called for a total investment of HK$231.90 million. This project also carried a guaranteed return.

The company would also acquire from CMCDI a 16.7 percent economic interest in a Sino-foreign cooperative joint venture which held the operating rights of the Luomei section of National Highway 324 in Guangdong province.
This toll road was expected to be completed in mid-1997.
The venture was established in June 1996 and had a term of 25 years and called for a total investment of HK$231.9 million. This project also carried a guaranteed return, it said.
The company would also acquire from Union Bank another 16.7 percent economic interest in the Luomei venture.

The listed company would also acquire from the parent a 23.73 percent equity interest in China International Marine Containers (Group) Ltd (CIMC), a Sino-foreign equity joint stock limited company which had class A and class B shares listed on the Shenzhen stock exchange.
The acquisitions would be funded by the issue of 650 million new shares at a price of HK$6.03 a share, raising a total of HK$3.86 billion, the statement said.
Trading in the shares of China Merchants was resumed on Thursday. The share closed HK$1.30 higher at HK$7.85.
